subject.title: Feature: Add maxTurns/maxToolCalls config option to limit agent iterations

question: Should OpenClaw add a global/per-agent hard iteration budget, and what counted unit and exhaustion behavior should become the permanent runtime contract?
rationale: The feature adds strict public configuration and changes terminal behavior during active model-tool execution, so maintainers must choose between tool-call, tool-round, timeout, and forced-summary semantics.

options.title: One hard tool-round budget
options.body: Count each model-to-tools round once, allow default and per-agent/subagent overrides, and stop with a defined final status when exhausted.

options.title: Separate call and time budgets
options.body: Expose independent total-call, round, and post-first-tool timeout controls at the cost of substantially more configuration and precedence complexity.

options.title: Keep heuristic guards
options.body: Rely on loop detection and whole-run timeouts, avoiding new configuration while leaving non-repetitive runaway usage uncapped.

recommendation.title: One hard tool-round budget
recommendation.body: Count each model-to-tools round once, allow default and per-agent/subagent overrides, and stop with a defined final status when exhausted.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history and prior issue review connect this person most directly to the current loop guard and unresolved product/API decision.
